usa.name: US Census Bureau cartographic boundaries, gazetteer, population estimates and metro delineations
usa.notes: Works of the US federal government are not subject to copyright (17 U.S.C. 105). Boundaries are the 2025 cartographic boundary files at 1:500,000 (generalised from TIGER/Line and clipped to the shoreline, so points in bays and coastal water fall in no county or place); ZIP Code Tabulation Areas exist only in the 2020 vintage, since ZCTAs are defined once per decennial census. ZCTAs approximate USPS ZIP Code delivery areas, which USPS does not publish as areas. Place populations are the Vintage 2025 Population Estimates (SUB-EST2025, July 2025) for incorporated places (and Urban Honolulu CDP, Hawaii having no incorporated places), and the American Community Survey 2020-2024 5-year estimates (table B01003, total population, from the table-based summary file, which needs no API key) for census-designated places and any place SUB-EST lacks; ZCTA populations are ACS too. CBSA and CSA membership is the July 2023 delineation (OMB Bulletin 23-01): list 1 for counties, list 2 for principal cities. Each ZCTA's postal city name is the city ZIP Code Business Patterns 2023 (County Business Patterns program) gives its ZIP Code, matched to a census place by name within the state, preferring places the 2020 ZCTA-to-place relationship file says overlap the ZCTA; ZIP Codes Business Patterns lacks are named from the other US postal source in postal.json. The files are NAD83 (EPSG:4269), used as WGS84: the two differ by 1-2 m in the US, within the generalisation of these files.

can.name: Statistics Canada, 2021 Census Boundary Files (cartographic)
can.credit: Adapted from Statistics Canada, 2021 Census Boundary Files (cartographic), reference date January 1, 2021. This does not constitute an endorsement by Statistics Canada of this product.
can.notes: Statistics Canada Open Licence (statcan.gc.ca/en/terms-conditions/open-licence); the credit is the licence's required notice for value-added products (the pack reprojects and simplifies the boundaries). Catalogue 92-160-X, reference guide 92-160-G. Cartographic files: clipped to the shoreline (coastal water belongs to no area) but not generalised, with a vertex every few metres; the build simplifies them (Douglas-Peucker, 10 m, per feature). Published only in Statistics Canada Lambert (EPSG:3347, NAD83); the build unprojects to longitude/latitude and uses NAD83 as WGS84 (1-2 m apart in Canada). The zips (Shapefile) sit on www12.statcan.gc.ca, which answers scripted downloads with a browser check (HTTP 403); 'service' is StatCan's own ArcGIS REST service of the same 2021 cartographic files (layers lpr_000b21s_e etc.), which the build can read instead (--via service). Names are StatCan's official forms, some bilingual ('Greater Sudbury / Grand Sudbury'). The Open Government Portal lists the same files under the Open Government Licence - Canada.

can.name: Statistics Canada, 2021 Census of Population, population and dwelling counts
can.credit: Adapted from Statistics Canada, Census of Population 2021, Population and dwelling counts (tables 98-10-0002-01, 98-10-0005-01 and 98-10-0019-01), reference date May 11, 2021. This does not constitute an endorsement by Statistics Canada of this product.
can.notes: Full-table CSV downloads. 98-10-0002-01 covers Canada, provinces and territories, census divisions and census subdivisions; 98-10-0005-01 CMAs and CAs (whole and by provincial part); 98-10-0019-01 forward sortation areas. Joined to the boundaries on DGUID. 63 CSDs (incompletely enumerated Indian reserves and settlements) have no count (symbol '..'); they are stored as null, not zero.
